data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: airplane
sections.question: airplane
sections.summary: a vehicle with wings and engines that flies through the air

senses.definition: a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that flies through the air carrying passengers or goods
examples: She took an airplane from London to New York for her holiday.
The airplane landed safely at the airport after a seven-hour flight.

answers.answer: She took an airplane from London to New York for her holiday.
He uses an airplane to go to the supermarket every Saturday morning.
She caught an airplane to cross the road to get to the park.
He parked his airplane outside his house every evening after work.

sections.title: airport
sections.question: airport
sections.summary: a place where airplanes take off and land, with buildings for passengers

senses.definition: a place where aeroplanes take off and land, with buildings where passengers wait
examples: She arrived at the airport two hours before her flight.
The airport was very busy because of the school holidays.

answers.answer: She arrived at the airport two hours before her flight departed.
He goes to the airport to buy fresh vegetables for dinner every week.
She goes to the airport to see the doctor about her sore throat.
He swims twenty laps at the airport every morning to keep fit.

sections.title: bicycle
sections.question: bicycle
sections.summary: a vehicle with two wheels that you ride by pushing pedals with your feet

senses.definition: a vehicle with two wheels that you ride by pushing the pedals with your feet
examples: She rides her bicycle to work every morning because she lives close to the office.
He bought a new bicycle to cycle along the river path at weekends.

answers.answer: She rides her bicycle to work every morning because she lives close to the office.
He uses his bicycle to fly to Paris for a business meeting.
She cooked dinner on her bicycle while riding home from work.
He swims across the lake on his bicycle every summer weekend.

sections.title: bus
sections.question: bus
sections.summary: a large road vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route

senses.definition: a large road vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route and stops at fixed places
examples: She takes the bus to school every morning because she does not have a car.
He missed the last bus and had to walk home in the rain.

answers.answer: She takes the bus to school every morning because she does not have a car.
He swims in the bus every morning to keep fit and stay healthy.
She cooked the family dinner in the bus because it has the biggest kitchen.
He plants flowers in the bus to make his garden look more beautiful.

sections.title: car
sections.question: car
sections.summary: a road vehicle with an engine, usually four wheels, for carrying a few people

senses.definition: a road vehicle with an engine and usually four wheels, used to carry a small number of people
examples: She drives her car to work every day because the office is far from her house.
He bought a second-hand car for five hundred pounds.

answers.answer: She drives her car to work every day because the office is far from her house.
He swims to work in his car every morning before breakfast.
She cooked a big meal in her car for the whole family on Sunday.
He planted vegetables in his car because it had the most space.

sections.title: journey
sections.question: journey
sections.summary: the act of travelling from one place to another

senses.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another, especially over a long distance
examples: The journey from London to Edinburgh by train takes about four hours.
She read a book during the long journey to keep herself busy.

answers.answer: The journey from London to Edinburgh by train takes about four hours.
She ate a big journey for lunch before going back to the office.
He drank his journey quickly before leaving the house that morning.
She cooked a journey in the kitchen for the whole family on Sunday.

sections.title: luggage
sections.question: luggage
sections.summary: the bags and suitcases you take with you when you travel

senses.definition: bags, suitcases, and other containers that you take with you when you travel
examples: She packed her luggage the night before her early morning flight.
He had so much luggage that he needed help to carry it all.

answers.answer: She packed her luggage the night before her flight to make sure she had everything.
He drank his luggage quickly at the café before getting on the train.
She cooked her luggage in the oven before leaving for the airport.
He grew luggage in his garden over the summer to prepare for his trip.

sections.title: map
sections.question: map
sections.summary: a drawing that shows the features of an area, town, or country

senses.definition: a drawing or diagram that shows the roads, rivers, towns, and other features of an area
examples: She used a map to find the way to the museum in the city.
He looked at the map to plan the best route for the road trip.

answers.answer: She used a map to find her way to the museum in the city centre.
He drank his map before getting on the train to stay warm.
She cooked the map in the oven for twenty minutes before dinner.
He ate his map at lunchtime because he was very hungry after the walk.

sections.title: station
sections.question: station
sections.summary: a place where trains or buses stop to let passengers get on or off

senses.definition: a place where trains or buses stop regularly so that passengers can get on or off
examples: She went to the station to catch the eight o'clock train to London.
He waited at the station for twenty minutes before the train arrived.

answers.answer: She went to the station to catch the eight o'clock train to London.
He goes to the station every Saturday to buy fresh vegetables for the week.
She swims in the station every morning to stay fit and healthy.
He cooks dinner at the station because it has the best kitchen in the area.

sections.title: taxi
sections.question: taxi
sections.summary: a car with a driver that you pay to take you to a place

senses.definition: a car with a driver that you pay to take you to a place you want to go
examples: She took a taxi to the hotel because she had too much luggage to walk.
He called a taxi because he missed the last bus home.

answers.answer: She took a taxi to the hotel because she had too much luggage to walk.
He went fishing in a taxi at the lake near his house on Sunday.
She cooked dinner in a taxi for the whole family on a rainy evening.
He planted flowers in a taxi to make his garden look more beautiful.
